notes.title: Sales, Sales, Sales! and Announcement on Development
notes.content:
[u][b]Hi everyone! It has been far too long.
[/b][/u]

Let me start off by apologizing for the lack of involvement and interaction in the game dev space. I have been stuck in some fairly aggressive schooling for the past 2 years (CPA Designation…) which has been taking up quite a bit of time. As a result, I have not been able to pump out my goal of 2 games per year, nor have I been able to spend much time, passion and energy in the development of any games in general.

I am happy to say that my final exam in next week (Wednesday to Friday – yes… a 3 day long final exam ☹) and after that, I am pleased to say that I can jump into the world of development once again!!

[u][b]Go forward projects:[/b][/u]

I have recently published Night at the Office (Late 2024) which is more of the traditional TurnVex style game.

My favorite game and my most advanced game is Snafu. Snafu has been an absolute blast to develop and is extremely unique. The reception the game has received is fantastic. Unfortunately, the spotlight out in the frontlines has been limited to the point where it’s fallen into the shadows quite fast. It’s unfortunate, but reality.

My goal for 2025 (and perhaps early 2026) is to develop the next Snafu with a focus on MMO style (without the online component). This approach is a big step up from what I am most comfortable with, but I believe it will be a fun project to work on. Similar to Snafu, it is not the traditional spooky house approach that most horror games are, but rather a unique approach that rarely ever sees the light of day. It may see the same fate as Snafu, falling out of the light quite fast, but it will be a blast to develop!

As always, I want to thank all my followers and those who have supported the journey of developing horror games! I look forward to jumping back into work within the next coming weeks to begin pumping out some spooky games to you all.

With that being said, to commemorate the end (hopefully…) of schooling, finally… All of my games will be 75% off for the week. 

Cheers! And happy gaming, everybody.

Stan. T

notes.title: Night at the Office - New Horror Game - Out This Friday
notes.content:
Happy December, everyone.

Just wanted to let you all know that my next horror game Night at the Office is now officially complete and is ready for launch this Friday the 13th. 

It's been a real pleasure developing Night at the Office, but there definitely were some challenges along the way.

It's been nearly two years since I've released a game, and that is mainly due to both work and school eating up a significant piece of 2023 and 2024, so it was a little difficult getting back into the slow stages of development, especially after releasing Snafu, which I believe to be one of my greatest concoctions. The bar was set quite high, in my opinion...

Nonetheless, Night at the Office takes a traditional approach which I have done in the past, however, with a bit more focus on story and puzzle aspects of the game.

It is always an honour to be able to build these games and push out what lingers in the imagination into a actual playable product; so to that, as always, I hope you all enjoy what Night at the Office has to offer when it releases this coming Friday. And if you could leave a review, providing me with your thoughts on what you enjoyed and/or disliked about the experience, I would greatly appreciate that!

Cheers, everybody and happy gaming.

notes.title: Is Simon There? is coming tomorrow!
notes.content:
Hello, everybody. I hope you are all doing very well.

I wanted to let you all know that my latest horror Is [u][b]Simon There?[/b][/u] will be releasing tomorrow at 10am PST / 11am Mountain time.

[u][b]Is Simon There?[/b][/u] will be slightly different from some of my more recent releases (i.e. Within Skerry and Inside Depth 6) in that it will focus primarily on creating an atmosphere for the player to dive into. 

[u][b]Is Simon There?[/b][/u] will have fewer [b]required puzzles[/b] (excluding optional puzzles) and fewer "aimless, eventless wandering". My goal is to tell a story while keeping you on the edge of your seat, while anticipating the next event to happen. 

Of course, like my previous games,[u] [b]Is Simon There?[/b][/u] will include 3 endings and 1 Easter Egg/ special ending. I've toned the difficulty of these optional puzzles down a little so that the vast majority of players can experience all the game has to offer without relying on too many guides. 

AND finally, no more getting knocked-out black screens. Nothing but silky smooth progression, a dark story, a neat little Easter Egg, and a hand full of intuitive puzzles to keep you thinking, throughout the 40 minute long journey. 

[u][b]Once again, Is Simon There? will be releasing tomorrow (May 06, 2022). And as always, if you play the game, please leave an honest review. I would love to know what you enjoyed and disliked about the game. [/b][/u]

Once [u][b]Is Simon There?[/b][/u] has been published, I will be spending some time researching new mechanics / systems to implement into new games (i.e. controller support, advanced AI, potential VR, etc)

Cheers, everybody!

Stan. T

notes.title: New horror - Inside Depth 6, Steam page now live!
notes.content:
[b]Hello everyone, I hope you are all doing well.
[/b]
I wanted to let everyone here know that [u][b]Inside Depth 6's Steam page is now LIVE![/b][/u]  After many months of development, I am very happy to say that the game is almost finished and ready to provide you all with some long awaited spooks.

I have learned a lot from Suite 776 and lots of the feedback received. I have taking this feedback very seriously and have applied the following to Inside Depth 6:
- Multiple endings,
- A random variant system (some events will trigger differently for everybody),
- Longer gameplay and a stronger focus on story,
- Significantly more exploration relative to Suite 776,
- More secrets and optional puzzles to take part in,
- and of course, an Easter egg; who doesn't love a little bit of Easter egg love?

[b]So what are my plans once Inside Depth 6 is released?[/b]
Once Inside Depth 6 is fully live, I intend to push out a couple of updates to the game within 1-2 months time. This is to scrub a couple of triggers, add a couple of additional areas to explore and a few additional scares.

Most of my time after launch will be focused on research. Due to Covid, I am focusing full time on Game development and Youtube, so this will allow me to focus on researching areas of game development like advanced AI, animations, and most importantly, for me, it gives me time to finally look into virtual reality (VR). It has been a long-awaited dream of mine to delve into some VR development, so now with all of this extra time to focus on game dev, I can allocate a lot of resources to VR research, And who knows, maybe I will be able to add VR support to Depth 6 and Suite 776 within the next several months.

Another area of importance for me is to research controller support and localization. I know that controller support and a lack of additional languages is a major negative to my titles, so I hope to implement some form of controller support and localization in the future - please bear with me on that! :)

So as always, I wish you all a safe and enjoyable 2021, happy gaming, stay safe, and I look forward to hearing from you all once Depth 6 has been released March 12!

Please feel free to provide some of your thoughts in the comments below :)

notes.title: The future of Minds Eyes
notes.content:
Hello everybody! Hopefully all is going well :)

This quick announcement is regarding the future of Minds Eyes and what is expected to come out of it in the future. The simple answer is nothing...

This game was released in 2016 as an experiment for the Steam community to try out [b]for free[/b] before I began publishing my larger projects. (Essentially a way to "Test the waters" prior to submitting main projects as this was my first attempt at Steam).

Because of that, the game is one of those "Take it as it is" games and will not be updated. 

One thing that most people fail to realize is that this game is not meant to have a storyline, or have any sense to it as it is an experiment testing multiple elements of horror in one single game. Regardless, the input provided by most of you was absolutely wonderful and has definitely aided me. To that, I thank you :)

Once again, I apologize for any inconvenience that this game may have caused! Despite being free??? Regardless, it was quite fun to build, and has provided me tons of input for my subsequent game - A Girls Fabric Face, and other upcoming horror games, too.

Many thanks everybody! and happy gaming :)

Stan.T

notes.title: My main project
notes.content:
Hello everyone! 

After quite a long time of development, creating 3D models, and coding pages upon pages of code; I am happy enough to present several screenshots of my main project for anyone who is interested.

If you arn't aware yet, the game is called: A Girls Fabric Face. I will not say anything about the story right now as it is still being developed; but all I can say is that it is extremely in depth and deep. 

One thing I want to make clear is that this game has absolutely nothing to do with Minds Eyes. Minds Eyes was just a test to gather input from everyone; thus no correlation between the two.

NOW! what are some main things that I added to this game; all of which are based on your inputs.

- The game being 90% interaction based rather than roughly 20% as Minds Eyes was.
- A large story is involved.
- Many puzzles and discoveries.
- A brand new mechanic; allowing you to view the premise from cameras set up around the house.
- House secrets and secret items.

notes.title: Main project suggestions
notes.content:
Alrighty everyone! I believe I’ve gotten enough criticism for this game by now! It is now time to begin working on the main project. Minds Eyes has definitely taught me a nice amount of things. I noticed that a lot of you enjoyed the game while some disliked the game as a whole (or some parts) which is good! Like I said before, Minds Eyes was made to gather information on new things which is why the game play have felt like 5 games in one. Ultimately, I am happy with the way things have gone. I’ve learned a lot, talked to a few people here and there, gotten a bit of support and some criticism here and there, too. 

SO! now it is time begin planning on the main project. I’ve been taking a lot of notes, beginning to sketch some models, as well as creating a full, in-depth storyline for you all to enjoy. I’ve been brainstorming ways to keep the player engaged most of the time, with a near complete elimination of ‘aimless wandering’ and more! 

To be completely honest, I’ve never really put the time to plan any of my games. Whenever I have a small idea, I simply expand on it, and make things on the go. This will definitely not be the case for this game. For the first time ever (in my time of publishing over 10 games), I will spend a large portion of time, brainstorming, modeling and creating the best horror experience that I am completely capable of doing. I will purchase a laptop so I can work at school as well, and involve as many people as I possibly can in brainstorming, researching and testing.

So what is this announcement particularly for? A discussion (in the announcement section). I want to talk to you all; I want to hear your ideas; I want to know what particularly scares you? What annoys you in a game? And what you would like to see in a game. It is my complete aim and goal to create something that I’ve never created before; a whole to level to my capabilities in order to raise my bar of standards to ultimately provide you all the best gaming experience possible.

As always, I thank you all for the support, and for some wonderful Ideas! Within a month or so, I believe I will begin posting some information on the new game, as well as screenshots, trailer, and more.

With that said, feel free to like me on facebook to get quick and early info on stuff!
https://www.facebook.com/turnvex/

Also, if you want to check out a nice little horror I’ve made a few months back, check out Dead Man’s Journey: 

http://gamejolt.com/games/dead-man-s-journey/139776

Once again! Thanks a bunch, and I’ll see you in the comments 

notes.title: That running animation though?
notes.content:
Let me start off by saying that the games mission was definitely fulfilled from just day 1. 
If you didn’t know, Minds Eyes was created in order to get a better understanding of what features you all enjoy in a game (horror to be specific). Did you enjoy having collectibles? Interacting with objects, interacting with MORE objects, trigger pauses, subtle changes to the home itself, and more.
From the videos I’ve seen so far, I believe I am able to say with quite certainty what I will include In my main project.
-	More interactions with the game.
-	Potentially include some collectibles 
-	Puzzles / problem solving
-	Drastically reducing “Aimlessly walking around for events to occur” 
-	Adding trigger paths which will trigger different events depending on where you are
-	And more along the way

Let me say thank you to all the people who support this game and truly understand its main purpose. I really appreciate the reviews, especially the negative, since they are definitely the ones that help me improve. I cannot guarantee that you will all enjoy my upcoming game, but I can guarantee that it is a drastic jump from anything I’ve ever made before. With my university beginning soon, I will be consumed with my accounting classes, thus limiting me to development quite some bit. On the bright site, it will give me me lots of time to begin planning, and truly focus on some wonderful horror elements!

As for that running animation; I truly do apologize for that! I just had to leave that in, I couldn’t restrain myself from removing such majestic qualities. 

Once again! Thank you all! And happy gaming!

Stan.T
